title: Bagan temple plain
summary: Bagan is a plain on a bend of the Ayeyarwady River in central Myanmar, the capital of the Pagan kingdom. Its kings, from Anawrahta onward, built a landscape of more than two thousand temples, stupas, monasteries and mounds, with the main building peak between the 11th and 13th centuries,, now a World Heritage property.

uncertainty.note: Start is the accession of Anawrahta (1044), whom Cooler calls the first historical ruler of Pagan; the temple-building peak that UNESCO dates to the 11th to 13th centuries follows. Cooler dates most major monuments to the century after his death. Pagan's origins reach back before the 9th century, so this marks the kingdom's consolidation, not the first settlement.

as_recorded.value: peak of Bagan civilization (11th -13th centuries CE)

importance.justification: A World Heritage sacred landscape and the capital of the first Burmese kingdom, with over two thousand surviving monuments (Cooler counts 2,230 buildings and mounds).

reviewer_note: Place pin only: no model. I found no heritage-body, museum or university page giving a height and plan size for one Bagan temple (Ananda or Shwesandaw), only encyclopedic or travel figures. Coordinates are the arithmetic mean of the seven UNESCO component points for property 1588, hence uncertainty_km 15; UNESCO gives no single site centre. Least sure: start year, a reign date standing for a multi-century process.
